title: Lower Shell Repair Area — Surface Preparation Before Protective Scheme Application
abstract: Cleaning and surface preparation of a lower shell repair area before a protective scheme is applied, including the water break test and the time limit between preparation and primer.

sections.purpose: This task prepares an aluminium or titanium surface in a lower shell repair area so that a protective scheme can be applied, and establishes by test that the surface is clean enough to accept it.
sections.job_setup_note: The time between the end of preparation and the start of priming is limited and the limit is short. Do not begin preparation until the primer is mixed, the operator is available and the area is masked. A prepared surface left overnight must be prepared again. Ventilation and extraction are needed throughout because the solvents are volatile.
sections.procedure: 1. Mask the area, including any bonding land and any fastener that must not be primed. 2. Remove the existing scheme locally by abrasion. Do not use a chemical stripper on a bonded joint or within fifty millimetres of a sealant fillet. WARNING: SOLVENT VAPOUR IS HEAVIER THAN AIR AND WILL COLLECT IN THE BILGE. VENTILATE AND EXTRACT AT THE LOWEST POINT OF THE COMPARTMENT. 3. Abrade the surface with the grade of pad given in the limits table, working in one direction only. 4. Remove the abrasion debris with a vacuum, not with compressed air. CAUTION: DO NOT BLOW THE AREA WITH COMPRESSED AIR. IT DRIVES DEBRIS UNDER THE MASKING AND INTO THE FASTENER HEADS. 5. Wipe with the approved solvent using a clean cloth for each pass, and change the cloth before it looks dirty. 6. Do the water break test: wet the surface and confirm that the film stays continuous for thirty seconds. 7. Where the film breaks, repeat the solvent wipe and test again. 8. Where the splice plate D5120114264366 or its left-hand equivalent D5120115552469 is in the area, check that no solvent has run into the joint. 9. Where the swaged collar LN40979-37 is present, mask it; the primer must not bridge the collar to the plate. 10. Record the time the water break test passed. 11. Apply the sol-gel preparation, where the scheme calls for it, within the time limit in the table. 12. Apply the primer within the second time limit. 13. Protect the protective sleeve AGS443655K5 at the harness pass-through from overspray.
sections.close_out: Record the water break test result and the times of preparation, sol-gel and primer. Where either time limit is exceeded, prepare the surface again from step 3. Remove the masking before the primer is fully cured, otherwise the edge will lift with it.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft; step 11 applies only where the chromate-free scheme is used

safety_precautions: Ventilate and extract at the lowest point of the compartment.
Do not use compressed air to clean the area.
Wear solvent-resistant gloves and eye protection.
